title.narrative: Improved accountability of public expenditure measured by the quality of annual financial reports (PI-25)

comment.narrative: The score B+ will be achieved. The target value for 2025 is a consolidated government statement is prepared annually and includes full information on revenue, expenditure and financial assets/liabilities. 14 TPSAS national standards are applied. MoF has introduced four new financial reporting forms, which comply with international standards.

actual.value: PEFA 2022 reports improvement in the score (now at B compared to C in PEFA 2017) for completeness of financing statements (PI-29.1), noting that the annual financial reports cover the majority of assets and liabilities (except the Public Investment Program and financial performance of state-owned enterprises). There is no changes since the last PEFA assessment. New financial reporting forms, complying withe international standards are introduced. Most likely, the score B+ will be achieved.

title.narrative: Improved accountability of public expenditures measured by the quality of financial audit (PI-26)

comment.narrative: PEFA 2022 reports a score of D+ compared to PEFA 2017 score of C+ (both using 2016 PEFA methodology) for the dimension external audit (now numbered PI-30) primarily due to the observation that the Chamber of Accounts is not fully independent. In terms of the target value for the indicator, latest data indicate it is on track to reach the target value for 2025. The target value for 2025 is: Audits cover central government entities representing at least 75% of total expenditures (2025). The target is achieved.

actual.value: Audit coverage of 75% of central government entities has been achieved , which complies with PEFA score B. Score B is final target of project.

title.narrative: Improved effectiveness of public expenditure measured by the increased alignment of expenditure with policy priorities (PI-12)

comment.narrative: Targets for 2021 and 2022, which provide that statements of sector strategies exist for several major sectors (2021) and sectoral strategies reports exist and are fully calculated on cost, generally consistent with financial projections, for sectors representing 25% of primary expenditures (2022) are achieved. Currently, 40% of budget expenditure is costed and aligned with sector priorities. There is a hope that 50% final target will be achieved by the project end date. The project intends to have a round table with MOF officials to agree on an action plan to achieve the final target.

actual.value: Improved effectiveness of public expenditure measured by the increased alignment of expenditure with policy priorities (PI-12) (Text, Custom) Baseline Actual (Previous) Actual (Current) End Target Value PEFA score D for PI-12 The Law of the Republic of Tajikistan “On Strategic Planning and State Forecasting” is adopted in May 25, 2022, It is expected that the new law will contribute to improvement of aligning of sectors priorities with budget expenditure. Currently the EU project is helping with capacity building in budget organizations on strategic planning. Currently, only the Ministry of Education, Ministry of Health and Ministry of Social Protection have their sector strategies, identified priorities and align their budget expenditures with priorities, which is about 40 percent of budget expenditure. The project regularly monitors progress with developing of this indicator.

title.narrative: Improved control of public expenditure measured by the stock of expenditure payment arrears (PI-4)

comment.narrative:
From baseline PEFA scores D PI-4, PEFA 2017 scores show improvements to C+ (using PEFA 2011 Methodology). PEFA 2022 reports a score of C+ for stock and monitoring of expenditure payment arrears no change from PEFA 2017 (both using the PEFA 2016 methodology and now numbered as PI-22 instead of PI-4). However, vis-a-vis the target values, the indicator is behind in publishing the information.
The target value of indicators in 2021 and 2023 are: data on stock of arrears is published (2021) and data on stock of arrears is published and it does not exceed 2% of total expenditure (2023). In 2023 the stock of arrears was less than 2% of budget expenditure. In 2024 the stock was less than 1% of budget arrears. The data on stock of arrears is still not published. There is no specific target for 2022. The data on 2025 is not available. Usually, the data is available at the end of FY.

actual.value: The stock of budget arrears in 2024 was less than 1%, which is PEFA score A. However, data on stock of arrears is not published. It is provided to external audit, the Government and the Parliament of Republic of Tajikistan.

title.narrative: Improved control of public expenditure measured by the stock of expenditure payment arrears (PI-4)

There is no specific target for 2022. In 2023 the stock of arrears was less than 2% of budget expenditure. In 2024 the stock was less than 1% of budget arrears. The data on 2025 is not available. Usually, the data is available at the end of FY. WB should use other instruments such as DPO or PforR to put a condition on publishing data on stock of arrear.

actual.value: The stock of budget arrears in 2024 was less than 1%, which is PEFA score A. However, data on stock of arrears is not published. It is provided to external audit, the Government and the Parliament of Republic of Tajikistan.

title.narrative: Additional functionalities (modules) of TFMIS (commitment control, cash management, payment order processing, assets management and payroll management) installed and operational

baseline.value: none of the 5 modules are operational

comment.narrative: The final target will be achieved. The final target values for this indicator are: 3 modules operational (2021) and 4 modules operational (2023). Currently (2025), the three modules of iMOF are functioning to differing extents: liability management is at around 90 percent, cash management with only plans input, and assets management is not active. Center of Financial Information Technologies (CFIT) has also developed a new accounting module under the TFMIS and this is linked with the iMOF. MOF has established a Working Group, consisting of CFIT, Central Treasury and Accounting Methodology Department, to make all four modules fully operational by the end 2025.

actual.value: The indicator is achievable. The three modules of iMOF are functioning to differing extents: liability management is at around 90 percent, cash management with only plans input, and assets management is not active. The project has funded the training of accountants from all 1,153 budget organizations for full operational implementation.

title.narrative: Beneficiaries satisfied with systems and procedures implemented by the Project, as measured by user satisfaction surveys (percent of users surveyed)

comment.narrative:

The target group of the survey were: the civil servants, suppliers or contractors of works and services, including procuring organizations, as well as the population of the Republic of Tajikistan. The total sample size was 1200 respondents almost double the baseline survey of 760 respondents.
The final target of 60% of indicator will be achieved.

title.narrative: Audits performed and audited financial statements submitted by largest SOEs

comment.narrative: No change from baseline. The indicator is behind the final target value, which is 50% based on financial statements are submitted to MOF by the end project in 2026. Currently, the draft Law of the Republic of Tajikistan “On Amendments and Additions to the Code of the Republic of Tajikistan on Administrative Offenses” has been developed with the view of establishing penalties for non-compliance with the requirements of legislation in the field of accounting, financial reporting and auditing by the business entities, which is under consideration by the Government of the Republic of Tajikistan. An independent audit firm was hired to audit the financial statements of the five largest state-owned enterprises for 2024 and provide capacity building on developing audit reports. It is expected that the Government amendments to the Law and capacity building activities will contribute to achieving final target for this indicator.

actual.value: Less than 30% - no change from baseline. The indicator, most likely, will not be achieved.

title.narrative: Audits performed and audited financial statements submitted by largest SOEs

Independent audit firm was hired to audit the financial statements of the five largest state-owned enterprises for 2024 and provide capacity building on developing audit reports. It is expected that the Government amendments to the Law and capacity building activities will contribute to achieving final target for this indicator, but it will take time. In potential new PFM project, WB should continue helping MoF with developing SOE's capacities with financial reporting.
